relevance_note: Case report of a GFAP-positive neonate plus a literature table of eight further coil 2B cases: "a female newborn with neonatal-onset Alexander disease caused by a heterozygous de novo point mutation c.1106T > C; p.(Leu369Pro)".
method_note: Built with a Python script in the scratch directory; table spans were cut programmatically from the raw Markdown (row label through the person's cell) and every span was checked verbatim. Index patient labelled 'patient' (rule 5); she is also the 'Case study' column (data column 1) of Table 3. Table 3 has patients as columns; header row: Case study | Knuutinen et al 9 | Paprocka et al 2 | Mura et al 8 | Takeuchi et al 3 | Li et al 4 (Pat. 32, Pat. 33, Pat. 35, Pat. 36); the Li et al columns use the printed labels 'Pat. 32' etc. (rule 1), the other literature columns are 'Table 3 column <k>'. The Discussion's description of the only other c.1106T > C case (ref 9, death at 6 weeks) is taken to be the Knuutinen column (Table 3 column 2), not a separate person. Table 1 (patients' MRI/CUS criteria; columns MRI DOL 4, MRI DOL 12, CUS DOL 11, CUS DOL 32) uses '+', '−' and '(+)'; the legend defines only NA, so '−' cells were not treated as excluded (rule 6, table symbols); '+' cells were recorded as observed. The two parents were tested by trio exome sequencing (variant de novo) and get rows as tested relatives, sex not stated, with no variant rows. 'in-depth laboratory tests were unremarkable' and 'no abnormal findings on prenatal ultrasound' are whole-investigation negatives, recorded as written and excluding nothing more specific. 'pregnancy and family history were unremarkable' was not recorded as a feature. Ages given as day of life ('First DOL', 'DOL 2', '4th DOL') and gestational ages were not converted to ISO durations. The paper calls the index variant a 'point mutation', which is not mapped to an enum class. n_patients_reported left null: the authors give no total. No stacked ' / ' cells. No contradictions found within the paper.
